skill.name: creating-agents
skill.description: Guides users through creating Claude Code subagents with clear roles, scoped tools, model choices, and reusable agent templates.
skill.summary: Create focused Claude Code subagents for task delegation, code review, research, and domain-specific workflows.
skill.author: BrendanShields

security_audit.summary: Static findings were reviewed in context and appear to be documentation false positives. The skill describes Claude Code agent creation, Markdown formatting, valid agent directories, and review templates without evidence of malicious execution, exfiltration, or prompt-injection intent.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples trigger static detectors for shell backticks.
remediation.suggestion: Consider adding prose that these are literal Markdown examples and not commands to execute.

remediation.issue: User-level agent paths use hidden home-directory locations.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that files should only be created at user request and only inside Claude agent directories.

remediation.issue: Some templates include Bash as an optional tool for generated agents.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend granting Bash only when a task requires command-line analysis or execution.

content.value_statement: Teams often need focused agents for review, research, and domain work. This skill provides a structured process and templates for creating Claude Code subagents with scoped tools.
actual_capabilities: Guides users through defining a subagent purpose and trigger conditions.
Explains project-level and user-level Claude Code agent storage locations.
Provides tool and model selection guidance for common agent types.
Shows the required Markdown and YAML frontmatter format for agent files.
Includes reusable reviewer, researcher, and specialist agent templates.
Documents proactive invocation patterns for automatic agent selection.
limitations: It provides guidance and templates, not an automated agent generator.
It is focused on Claude Code subagents, not general chatbot frameworks.
Generated agents still need review before use in sensitive projects.
Tool permissions must be adjusted manually for each workflow.

use_cases.title: Create a Code Review Agent
use_cases.description: Define a read-only reviewer that checks quality, security, reliability, and maintainability before merge.

use_cases.title: Build a Codebase Research Agent
use_cases.description: Create an agent that searches files, reads relevant code, and summarizes architecture with file references.

use_cases.title: Design a Domain Specialist Agent
use_cases.description: Create a focused specialist for databases, APIs, testing, or another technical area with tailored tools.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple read-only helper.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a Claude Code subagent for codebase research. Ask me for the purpose, trigger phrases, storage location, tools, and model before drafting the agent file.

prompt_templates.title: Scope Agent Tools
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose safe tool permissions for a known task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a code review subagent. Recommend the smallest useful tool set, explain the model choice, and draft the system prompt with clear review boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Customize a Specialist
prompt_templates.scenario: Adapt the specialist template to a project domain.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a database specialist subagent for this repository. Include trigger conditions, tool permissions, domain responsibilities, constraints, and an output format.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Agent Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before installing an agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed Claude Code agent definition for excessive permissions, unclear triggers, prompt conflicts, and missing boundaries. Suggest a safer final version.

output_examples.input: Create a read-only research agent for an unfamiliar codebase.
output_examples.output: A complete agent definition with a clear researcher role, Read, Glob, and Grep tools, haiku model guidance, and an output format for file-backed findings.

output_examples.input: Help me decide whether my agent needs Bash.
output_examples.output: A permission recommendation that compares read-only tools with command execution and explains when Bash is justified.

output_examples.input: Make a proactive code review agent.
output_examples.output: A reviewer agent draft with trigger wording, scoped review categories, severity labels, and instructions to provide file and line references.

best_practices: Give each agent one clear purpose and explicit trigger conditions.
Grant the smallest tool set that supports the intended task.
Review generated agent prompts before storing them in project or user agent directories.
anti_patterns: Do not give every agent full tool access by default.
Do not create broad agents with unclear ownership or overlapping triggers.
Do not store project-specific agents in the user directory when the team should share them.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It helps draft Claude Code subagent definitions, including purpose, triggers, tools, model choice, and system prompt content.

faq.question: Does it automatically install agents?
faq.answer: No. It explains where agent files belong and provides templates, but users control file creation and installation.

faq.question: Which tools should a new agent receive?
faq.answer: Start with Read, Glob, and Grep for analysis. Add Write, Edit, Bash, or Task only when the workflow requires them.

faq.question: Can this skill help with proactive agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to write descriptions with clear trigger conditions so Claude can select an agent automatically.

faq.question: Is this useful outside Claude Code?
faq.answer: The main format targets Claude Code. Some prompt design principles can still help with Codex or other agent workflows.

faq.question: What should I review before using a generated agent?
faq.answer: Check the trigger description, tool permissions, model choice, and boundaries against the actual task and repository risk.
